supported launcher from the\\\\nrepository root:\\\\n\\\\n```sh\\\\nPORT=8080 ./run.sh\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`run.sh` runs `go run .` in the foreground. The server initializes its local\\\\ndatabase and listens only on `127.0.0.1:$PORT`; if `PORT` is unset, it uses\\\\n`8080`. A running instance can be checked with:\\\\n\\\\n```sh\\\\ncurl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/health\\\\ngo test ./...\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThere are currently no Go test files, so `go test ./...` is also the package\\\\ncompile check. Do not start a long-running server as part of automated\\\\nverification.\\\\n\\\\n## Implementation map\\\\n\\\\nThe application is intentionally a single `main` package with no third-party\\\\nGo dependencies:\\\\n\\\\n- `main.go` contains the entry point, domain models, routing, HTTP handlers,\\\\n  persistence adapter, validation, and JSON response helpers.\\\\n- `main` initializes storage before binding the HTTP server.\\\\n- `newRouter` is the complete public routing inventory. Its method-qualified\\\\n  `http.ServeMux` patterns are the source of truth for accepted endpoints.\\\\n- `run.sh` is the foreground launcher.\\\\n- `go.mod` declares module `dndrest` and Go 1.26.\\\\n\\\\nWithin `main.go`, handlers are arranged by domain: rules and character\\\\ncalculations; combat; authentication; playable campaigns and turn flow;\\\\nstorage administration; compendium content; campaign management; and DM\\\\nutilities. Shared helpers near the end implement strict request decoding and\\\\nJSON responses.\\\\n\\\\n## State, persistence, and routing\\\\n\\\\n`game.db` is created in the current working directory. The storage adapter\\\\nuses the system `/usr/bin/sqlite3` executable and stores JSON documents for\\\\nthe domain records, alongside indexed identifiers and a few relational\\\\nconstraints. `schemaDefinition` is shared by startup and reset so both paths\\\\ncreate the same tables. The `GET /v1/storage/status` and\\\\n`POST /v1/storage/reset` endpoints expose the established storage lifecycle.\\\\n\\\\nUsers and combat sessions are loaded into mutex-protected in-memory maps at\\\\nstartup and persisted after writes. Other resources are read from SQLite per\\\\nrequest. `storageState` serializes database access. When a reset needs all\\\\nstate locks, it takes them in this order: user state, combat state, then\\\\nstorage state. Preserve that order in code that holds more than one of them.\\\\n\\\\nThe router exposes these main API groupings:\\\\n\\\\n- `/health` and `/v1/storage/*` for liveness and storage administration.\\\\n- `/v1/dice`, `/v1/checks`, `/v1/characters`, `/v1/encounters`,\\\\n  `/v1/initiative`, and `/v1/phb` for deterministic rules helpers.\\\\n- `/v1/combat/sessions` and `/v1/auth` for combat state and account access.\\\\n- `/v1/compendium/*` for monsters and items.\\\\n- `/v1/campaigns/*` for campaigns, characters, events, inventory, equipment,\\\\n  factions, NPCs, quests, downtime, scheduling, audit/export, and analytics.\\\\n- `/v1/play/campaigns/*` for owner/player membership, campaign documents,\\\\n  narration, turn state, actions, resolutions, and nudges.\\\\n- `/v1/dm/*` for encounter, loot, and recap tools.\\\\n\\\\n## Safe extension and testing conventions\\\\n\\\\nThe API is a compatibility contract. Preserve each route's method and path,\\\\nstatus code, response field ordering/shape, validation rule and message, and\\\\npersistence behavior. Add any future route to `newRouter` using a\\\\nmethod-qualified pattern rather than introducing manual method dispatch.\\\\n\\\\nDecode bodies with `decodeJSON`: it limits bodies to 1 MiB, rejects unknown\\\\nfields, and rejects trailing JSON values. Write JSON with `respondJSON` or\\\\n`badRequest` so the existing content type and error shape remain consistent.\\\\nKeep validation and ordering deterministic. For persistence changes, test\\\\nsuccessful and invalid requests plus restart and reset behavior in an isolated\\\\nworking directory, because `game.db` is intentionally durable across process\\\\nstarts. Run `gofmt -w main.go` and `go test ./...` before handing off Start it in the foreground from the repository\\\\\\\\nroot:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```sh\\\\\\\\nPORT=8080 ./run.sh\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe process binds only to `127.0.0.1:$PORT` (and defaults to port `8080` when\\\\\\\\n`PORT` is unset). Do not\\\\\\\\nstart a long-running server as part of automated verification.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Implementation map\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`main.go` is the complete application package:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- `main` initializes persisted state, selects the port, and starts `net/http`.\\\\\\\\n- `newRouter` is the public routing inventory. Each entry is a method-qualified\\\\\\\\n  `http.ServeMux` pattern and maps directly to its handler.\\\\\\\\n- The handlers are grouped by domain: core dice/check/character helpers;\\\\\\\\n  combat sessions; authentication; storage administration; compendium monsters\\\\\\\\n  and items; campaign state; PHB rules; and DM tools.\\\\\\\\n- The storage helpers (`initializeStorage`, schema functions, `runSQLite`, and\\\\\\\\n  `querySQLite`) own the file-backed persistence boundary.\\\\\\\\n- The small helpers at the bottom handle strict JSON decoding and JSON error/\\\\\\\\n  success responses.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`run.sh` is the supported launcher and deliberately runs `go run .` in the\\\\\\\\nforeground. `go.mod` pins the module to Go 1.26 with no third-party Go\\\\\\\\ndependencies.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## State and persistence\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`game.db` is created in the current working directory. The storage adapter\\\\\\\\ninvokes `/usr/bin/sqlite3` and stores users, combat sessions, compendium\\\\\\\\nrecords, campaigns, campaign characters, and campaign events. JSON blobs are\\\\\\\\nused for structured records; users and combat sessions are also loaded into\\\\\\\\nthe process-local maps during startup. The storage status and reset endpoints\\\\\\\\nexpose the existing schema lifecycle.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThree mutex-protected state areas exist: user state, combat state, and storage\\\\\\\\nstate. Where reset needs all three, it locks user state, then combat state,\\\\\\\\nthen storage state. Code that touches multiple areas must preserve this order\\\\\\\\nto avoid deadlocks. Persistence helpers called while user or combat state is\\\\\\\\nheld acquire only the storage mutex.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Safe extension conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPreserve the existing API contract exactly: method, route pattern, status code,\\\\\\\\nJSON shape, validation message, and persistence behavior are observable.\\\\\\\\nRegister any accepted new route in `newRouter`; keep method-qualified patterns\\\\\\\\ninstead of adding ad-hoc method checks. Decode request bodies through\\\\\\\\n`decodeJSON`, which enforces a 1 MiB limit, rejects unknown fields, and rejects\\\\\\\\ntrailing JSON values. Send responses through `respondJSON` or `badRequest` to\\\\\\\\nretain the JSON content type and error format.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nKeep validation deterministic, use the existing storage helpers for durable\\\\\\\\nrecords, and test both successful and invalid requests. For persistence work,\\\\\\\\nalso verify restart and reset behavior using an isolated working directory so\\\\\\\\nthe local `game.db` does not leak state between test runs.\\\\\\\\nmodule \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"invalid rest\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\")\\\\\\\\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\\\\\\\\nset -euo pipefail\\\\\\\\ngo run .\\\\\\\\nmodule dndrest\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\ngo 1.26\\\\\\\\n# D&D REST API\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Running and verifying\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe service requires Go 1.26 and the system `sqlite3` executable used by the\\\\\\\\nexisting persistence adapter. Start it in the foreground from the repository\\\\\\\\nroot:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```sh\\\\\\\\nPORT=8080 ./run.sh\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe process binds only to `127.0.0.1:$PORT` (and defaults to port `8080` when\\\\\\\\n`PORT` is unset). With it running, a quick health check is:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```sh\\\\\\\\ncurl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/health\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBefore changing code, use `gofmt -w main.go` and `go test ./...`; the package\\\\\\\\ncurrently has no Go test files, so the latter is also a compile check. Do not\\\\\\\\nstart a long-running server as part of automated verification.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Implementation map\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`main.go` is the complete application package:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- `main` initializes persisted state, selects the port, and starts `net/http`.\\\\\\\\n- `newRouter` is the public routing inventory. Each entry is a method-qualified\\\\\\\\n  `http.ServeMux` pattern and maps directly to its handler.\\\\\\\\n- The handlers are grouped by domain: core dice/check/character helpers;\\\\\\\\n  combat sessions; authentication; storage administration; compendium monsters\\\\\\\\n  and items; campaign state; PHB rules; and DM tools.\\\\\\\\n- The storage helpers (`initializeStorage`, schema functions, `runSQLite`, and\\\\\\\\n  `querySQLite`) own the file-backed persistence boundary.\\\\\\\\n- The small helpers at the bottom handle strict JSON decoding and JSON error/\\\\\\\\n  success responses.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`run.sh` is the supported launcher and deliberately runs `go run .` in the\\\\\\\\nforeground. `go.mod` pins the module to Go 1.26 with no third-party Go\\\\\\\\ndependencies.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## State and persistence\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`game.db` is created in the current working directory. The storage adapter\\\\\\\\ninvokes `/usr/bin/sqlite3` and stores users, combat sessions, compendium\\\\\\\\nrecords, campaigns, campaign characters, and campaign events. JSON blobs are\\\\\\\\nused for structured records; users and combat sessions are also loaded into\\\\\\\\nthe process-local maps during startup. The storage status and reset endpoints\\\\\\\\nexpose the existing schema lifecycle.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThree mutex-protected state areas exist: user state, combat state, and storage\\\\\\\\nstate. Where reset needs all three, it locks user state, then combat state,\\\\\\\\nthen storage state. Code that touches multiple areas must preserve this order\\\\\\\\nto avoid deadlocks. Persistence helpers called while user or combat state is\\\\\\\\nheld acquire only the storage mutex.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Safe extension conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPreserve the existing API contract exactly: method, route pattern, status code,\\\\\\\\nJSON shape, validation message, and persistence behavior are observable.\\\\\\\\nRegister any accepted new route in `newRouter`; keep method-qualified patterns\\\\\\\\ninstead of adding ad-hoc method checks. Decode request bodies through\\\\\\\\n`decodeJSON`, which enforces a 1 MiB limit, rejects unknown fields, and rejects\\\\\\\\ntrailing JSON values.
